comments.body:
At a4295af, `platform` is still not explicit-only when it comes from the environment. With `AGENT_DEVICE_PLATFORM=ios` set and no `--platform`, the parser strips it, then `applyDefaultPlatformBinding` re-adds it from the env ([session-binding.ts#L36-L38](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/a4295af/src/session-binding.ts#L36-L38)) before `device` reads `flags.platform` ([device.ts#L24](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/a4295af/src/cli/commands/device.ts#L24)). So `device status --serial emulator-5560` still filters claims by platform in that setup. A config `platform` is not affected. Should every command that lists `platform` in `explicitOnlyFlags` skip that binding step, or should `platform` leave the list if the env case is acceptable? Please cover whichever you choose with a test that runs through the `cli.ts` route with `AGENT_DEVICE_PLATFORM` set. I read the code path but did not run it, and I did not trace whether `lockPolicy` is set for device runs by default.

Not blocking: the case in `resolve-cli-options.test.ts` ([L115](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/a4295af/src/cli/resolve-cli-options.test.ts#L115)) only calls `resolveCliOptions` with an empty env, so it cannot see the binding step. Adding `AGENT_DEVICE_PLATFORM`, `UDID` and `SERIAL` cases through `runCli` would close that gap, and you can take or leave it.

The two open inline threads still apply: [env default untested](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4314#discussion_r4502092304) and [platform re-added after parse](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4314#discussion_r4502092305). CI is green with 11 checks and none failing, and there are no conflicts. Before merge, platform must stay explicit-only past `applyDefaultPlatformBinding` (or leave the list), with the env case covered through `runCli`.

Platform stays explicit-only. `device` lists `platform` in `explicitOnlyFlags`, and that list already says a config or env default must not narrow claims, so any command that lists `platform` there skips `applyDefaultPlatformBinding`. With no session configured, `lockPolicy` is unset, which is why the binding step was running and putting `AGENT_DEVICE_PLATFORM` back before `device` read `flags.platform`. A typed `--platform` still filters. The new test goes through `runCli`: `device status --serial emulator-5560` with `AGENT_DEVICE_PLATFORM=ios` and no `--platform` keeps the android claim, and the same command with `--platform ios` hides it.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

With no session configured, `lockPolicy` is unset, which is why the binding step was running and putting `AGENT_DEVICE_PLATFORM` back before `device` read `flags.platform`. A typed `--platform` still filters. The new test goes through `runCli`: `device status --serial emulator-5560` with `AGENT_DEVICE_PLATFORM=ios` and no `--platform` keeps the android claim, and the same command with `--platform ios` hides it.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Thanks for the update. At e6bdebf the explicit-only `platform` binding from the [earlier review](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4314#issuecomment-6708409518) is fixed, and the new `runCli` case with `AGENT_DEVICE_PLATFORM=ios` covers it. One path is still open. All 11 reported checks pass or are skipped, and there are no conflicts. Before merge, the saved-connection path below needs a fix. Note that #4315 fixes the same issue (#4298), including this path, so only one of the two should merge.

Saved remote-connection defaults can still narrow `device status` and `device release`. `mergeConnectionFlags` still merges active connection defaults into `effectiveFlags` ([src/cli.ts:848](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/e6bdebf/src/cli.ts#L848)), and `resolveActiveConnectionDefaults` does not skip `device`. If the saved state stores a platform (`state.platform ?? profile.platform`), `agent-device device status --serial X` or `device release --stale` reads that platform and filters the claim query by a value the caller did not type. That is the same failure as #4298: claims on other platforms disappear, and `device release --stale` reports 'No local device claims matched'. The parser comment names remote-config defaults as a source that explicit-only flags must ignore. I traced this from the code and did not run it with a real connection state. The rule to enforce: for a command that declares `explicitOnlyFlags`, only the command line may supply those keys once `effectiveFlags` is built. Please enforce it once, after binding and `mergeConnectionFlags`, and add a `runCli` case with a saved connection state that stores a platform.

Could the `includes('platform')` branch in `cli.ts` go away? After `effectiveFlags` is computed, delete every `explicitOnlyFlags` key that is not in `explicitFlagKeys`, reusing the parser's strip helper. That covers env binding, connection defaults and any later merge for every command that declares the list, including `settings` targetApp, with about the same line count. A narrower option is to skip `device` in `resolveActiveConnectionDefaults`, as #4315 does. Nothing has to change first except exporting or moving the strip helper.

Not blocking: the config test in `resolve-cli-options.test.ts` calls `resolveCliOptions` only, and the `runCli` test covers env only for platform, so env or connection-supplied device, udid and serial are not asserted end to end. The parser strip is uniform across keys, so this is a coverage gap and not a failing path. You can add `AGENT_DEVICE_UDID`/`AGENT_DEVICE_SERIAL` to the `runCli` test, or leave it.

On the open inline threads: the one on [the remote-connection merge path](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4314#discussion_r4502092305) still applies and is covered by the paragraph above. The one on [UDID and SERIAL env cases](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/pull/4314#discussion_r4502092304) can be resolved: the platform case is now covered, and the rest is the optional coverage note above.

I did not execute any code. The new test's validity and the connection-merge path come from reading the PR-head code.

#4315 has merged and fixes #4298 for config, env and saved-connection defaults, and this PR now conflicts with main. Thank you for the work here. Unless something in this PR is still missing from main, it can be closed.
